{"content": "Below is a concise guide on how to create a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance with a GPU (e.g., NVIDIA RTX A6000 or closest available) running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.

---

## 1. Prerequisites
- **Google Cloud SDK** installed (`gcloud` CLI).
- **Billing** enabled on your project.
- **Compute Engine API** enabled.
- Appropriate IAM permissions (e.g., `roles/compute.admin`).

## 2. Choose a GPU type
Google Cloud currently offers NVIDIA GPUs such as:
- `nvidia-tesla-t4`
- `nvidia-tesla-p100`
- `nvidia-tesla-v100`
- `nvidia-tesla-a100`

If you specifically need an RTX A6000, check if it's available in your region; otherwise, use the nearest equivalent (e.g., `nvidia-tesla-a100`).

## 3. Create the instance via gcloud CLI
```bash
# Set your project and zone
PROJECT_ID="your-project-id"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="my-gpu-instance"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"   # Adjust CPU/RAM as needed
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a100"   # Replace with your desired GPU type
GPU_COUNT=1
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create $INSTANCE_NAME \
  --project=$PROJECT_ID \
  --zone=$ZONE \
  --machine-type=$MACHINE_TYPE \
  --accelerator=type=$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT \
  --image-family=$IMAGE_FAMILY \
  --image-project=$IMAGE_PROJECT \
  --boot-disk-size=50GB \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --metadata startup-script='#!/bin/bash
apt-get update
apt-get install -y build-essential dkms
# Install NVIDIA drivers
curl -s -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/compute-image-packages/master/scripts/install-driver.sh | bash
'
```

### Explanation of flags
- `--machine-type`: Defines CPU & RAM.
- `--accelerator`: Adds GPU(s).
- `--image-family` + `--image-project`: Specifies Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.
- `--boot-disk-size`: Size of the boot disk.
- `--startup-script`: Installs NVIDIA drivers automatically.

## 4. Verify the instance
```bash
# List instances
gcloud compute instances list --project=$PROJECT_ID --zone=$ZONE

# SSH into the instance
gcloud compute ssh $INSTANCE_NAME --project=$PROJECT_ID --zone=$ZONE

# Inside the VM, verify GPU
nvidia-smi
```

## 5. REST API (optional)
If you prefer to use the REST API directly:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
    "machineType": "projects/'$PROJECT_ID'/zones/'$ZONE'/machineTypes/'$MACHINE_TYPE'",
    "disks": [
      {
        "boot": true,
        "autoDelete": true,
        "initializeParams": {
          "sourceImage": "projects/'$IMAGE_PROJECT'/global/images/family/'$IMAGE_FAMILY'",
          "diskSizeGb": 50
        }
      }
    ],
    "networkInterfaces": [
      {
        "network": "global/networks/default",
        "accessConfigs": [{"type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT"}]
      }
    ],
    "guestAccelerators": [
      {
        "acceleratorType": "projects/'$PROJECT_ID'/zones/'$ZONE'/acceleratorTypes/'$GPU_TYPE'",
        "acceleratorCount": $GPU_COUNT
      }
    ],
    "serviceAccounts": [
      {
        "email": "default",
        "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

## 6. Cleanup
```bash
# Delete the instance when done
gcloud compute instances delete $INSTANCE_NAME --project=$PROJECT_ID --zone=$ZONE
```

---

**Note:** Always double-check the availability of the GPU type in your chosen zone. You can list available GPUs with:
```bash
gcloud compute accelerator-types list --project=$PROJECT_ID --zone=$ZONE
```
